record.paper_title: Quantum Communication: From Fundamentals to Recent Trends, Challenges and Open Problems
record.original_question: How should quantum internet network designs scale across both long-distance users and compact processor-or-circuit settings while managing computational complexity in entanglement distribution and selecting entanglement-distribution guidelines based on user requirements and hardware configuration?

evidence.quote: Finally, there are certain network design challenges that are of interest to quantum communication engineers. The work in [309] investigate the scalability of quantum internet for scenarios when the users are separated over long distances or within a small space over a processor or circuit within a same framework.

Similarly, the authors in [310] consider computational complexity for entanglement distributions in quantum networks. In [311], the authors provide a set of guidelines on using entanglement distribution based on user requirements and hardware configuration.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a quantum communication network modeled as a graph G=(V,E) in which each vertex represents a quantum node (a user terminal, a repeater, or a qubit register within a single processor/circuit) and each edge represents a physical channel capable of generating bipartite entangled pairs at a known rate with a known fidelity. An entanglement-distribution protocol specifies, for each requested end-to-end entanglement demand (s_i,t_i,r_i,F_i) — source, target, required rate, required fidelity — a scheduling of elementary entanglement generations, entanglement swappings, and purifications across G.

Develop a unified framework for designing scalable entanglement-distribution protocols on G that simultaneously addresses the following questions:

(a) Provide a single protocol family that performs efficiently both in the long-distance regime (where |V| is large, edges are lossy, and repeater chains dominate) and in the on-chip/short-distance regime (where nodes correspond to qubits inside one processor and decoherence rather than loss is the limiting resource), with provable performance guarantees in each regime.

(b) Characterize the computational complexity of optimal entanglement distribution: given G, a set of demands, and per-edge generation/swap/purification parameters, determine the complexity class of computing a schedule that maximizes aggregate end-to-end entanglement rate subject to fidelity constraints, and identify approximation algorithms with provable ratios or hardness-of-approximation results.

(c) Produce a rigorous set of guidelines — i.e., a decision procedure mapping (user demands, hardware parameters such as gate fidelity, memory coherence time, channel loss, swap success probability) to a recommended distribution strategy (e.g., direct transmission, repeater chain with nested purification, multipath routing, all-photonic schemes) — together with a proof that following the guideline yields performance within a specified factor of optimum across the stated parameter ranges.

The problem is to formulate and solve (a)–(c) within one mathematical model.
artifact.status_search_result: Scalable entanglement-distribution network design remains an active open research area as of 2026. Partial results exist for routing and complexity of entanglement distribution (e.g., NP-hardness of certain entanglement-routing problems and heuristic/approximation algorithms), and various works provide hardware-dependent guidelines, but no single unified framework simultaneously addresses long-distance and on-chip scaling with provable complexity and guideline guarantees.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of entanglement distribution
status_evidence.snippet: Studies hardness and algorithms for entanglement distribution in quantum networks.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of entanglement distribution is studied with partial hardness results, but a unified scalable framework is not established.

status_evidence.title: Guidelines for entanglement distribution
status_evidence.snippet: Provides parameter-dependent recommendations for entanglement distribution strategies based on hardware.
status_evidence.claim: Guidelines exist but are heuristic and not unified with complexity-theoretic guarantees.
